paper.title: An Index-based Deterministic Asymptotically Optimal Algorithm for Constrained Multi-armed Bandit Problems

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained multi-armed bandit (CMAB): identify an epsilon-optimal feasible set
unmapped: Each pull yields both a reward sample and an independent cost sample; arm a is feasible iff its mean cost C_a <= C, for a constant threshold C known to the learner
Goal: output an epsilon-optimal set (arms that are approximately feasible and approximately reward-optimal among feasible arms), with a fixed budget of T pulls
The learner knows the optimal feasible mean mu* = max_{a feasible} mu_a (CAPT)
settings.definition_quote: We define the feasible set A_f of arms such that A_f := { a in A | C_a <= C } for a constant C known to the player and assume that A_f \neq \emptyset. Our goal is to find an optimal feasible arm that achieves the optimal value mu^*:=max_{a in A_f} mu_a.

symbols.H_eps: complexity H(epsilon) = sum_a min(Delta_a^eps, Phi_a^eps)^{-2}, where Delta_a^eps = |mu_a - mu*| + eps and Phi_a^eps = |C_a - C| + eps
symbols.eps_tol: tolerance epsilon > 0 used by the algorithm and in the definition of epsilon-optimal set

conditions: reward and cost distributions supported in [0,1]
tuning: epsilon > 0 is the algorithm's tolerance parameter

source.label: thm1
source.quote: Assume that the reward and the cost distributions associated with all arms in $A$ have the support in $[0,1]$. Then for any $\epsilon > 0$ and $T\geq 2|A|$, the output $A_T^*(\epsilon) \cap A_T^f(\epsilon)$ by CAPT at $T$ satisfies \[ \Pr\{ A^{\epsilon}_* \cap A^{-\epsilon}_f \subseteq  A_T^*(\epsilon)  \cap A_T^f(\epsilon)  \subseteq A^{-\epsilon}_* \cap A^{\epsilon}_f \} \geq 1 - 2|A|T e^{-T/16H(\epsilon)}.\]

results.notes: The bound is on the probability that the output is not an epsilon-optimal set, which is 1 minus the stated success probability. The final line of the proof gives exp(-2T/16H), which is tighter; the expression recorded here is the one in the theorem statement. Section 4 only argues informally that CAPT-E converges asymptotically, so no result is recorded for CAPT-E.
